I am 66 years old, and I have worked this land in Quzhou for 35 years. My wife and I are the only ones left at home—our children have jobs in the city. With just the two of us and 10.1 mu to manage, I cannot afford to take risks or waste labor. I know this soil like the back of my hand, and I stick to what works.

For winter wheat, I will plant the full 10.1 mu after the maize comes off. I will buy improved wheat seed from the supply store; the old traditional seeds simply cannot compete anymore. Before sowing, I will run the rotary tiller to break up the maize stubble and prepare a good seedbed. I will spread compound fertilizer as a basal dose, then topdress with urea in the spring when the wheat greens up. Using my well, I will irrigate three times: once after sowing to help establishment, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I will spray three times in total—herbicide early and insecticide when the aphids appear. If the weather holds, I expect about 1,000 jin per mu, or roughly 1,000 kg/mu.

For summer maize, I will plant the same 10.1 mu immediately after wheat harvest in June. There is barely a week between crops, so I will use no-tillage direct seeding—there is no time to plough, and the wheat stubble helps keep moisture in. I will plant hybrid seed, Denghai 605 or something similar, because everyone around here has switched to hybrid; the yield is just too much better. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and maybe a bit of extra nitrogen later if the plants look pale. I will irrigate twice: at sowing if the soil is dry, and again at the big trumpet stage. I will spray three times—herbicide and insecticide for corn borers. I expect around 1,100 kg/mu if the summer rains cooperate.
